deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page applies the same device as the previous page (where Ramanujan found B = -gamma in sum_{p<x} log p/(p-1) = log x + B + o(1)). The device is to compare the constant term of a Dirichlet series as s->1+ with the constant term of the corresponding partial sum at s=1. Here the target is the constant in the asymptotic for sum_{n<x} d(n)/n. Ramanujan's gamma_1 is the negative of the modern Stieltjes constant: gamma_1(R) = -gamma_1(Stieltjes) = 0.0728158454836767...

(1) sum_{n<x} log n/n = (1/2) log^2 x - gamma_1 + o(1). In modern terms this is the defining limit of the first Stieltjes constant, gamma_1(Stieltjes) = lim [sum_{n<=x} log n/n - (1/2) log^2 x], with the sign flipped.

(2) zeta(s) = 1/(s-1) + gamma + gamma_1 (s-1) + o(s-1). Hence -zeta'(s) = sum log n/n^s = 1/(s-1)^2 - gamma_1 + o(1).

(3) Squaring gives zeta(s)^2 = 1/(s-1)^2 + 2gamma/(s-1) + gamma^2 + 2gamma_1 + o(1). Also zeta(s)^2 = sum d(n)/n^s.

(4) From (2) and the expansion of zeta: sum (2gamma + log n)/n^s = 2gamma zeta(s) - zeta'(s) = 1/(s-1)^2 + 2gamma/(s-1) + 2gamma^2 - gamma_1 + o(1).

(5) Subtracting (3) from (4): the poles cancel, and sum (2gamma + log n - d(n))/n^s -> gamma^2 - 3gamma_1 as s->1+.

(6) From (1) and sum_{n<x} 1/n = log x + gamma + o(1): sum_{n<x} (2gamma + log n)/n = (1/2) log^2 x + 2gamma log x + 2gamma^2 - gamma_1 + o(1).

(7) Assume Dirichlet's divisor theorem, sum_{n<x} d(n) = x(log x + 2gamma - 1) + O(sqrt x). Partial summation then gives sum_{n<x} d(n)/n = (1/2) log^2 x + 2gamma log x + B + o(1).

Conclusion. By (6) and (7), sum a_n/n converges with a_n = 2gamma + log n - d(n), and its sum is 2gamma^2 - gamma_1 - B. [My gloss, implicit in the text: Abel's theorem for Dirichlet series then says sum a_n/n^s tends to the same value as s->1+.] Comparing with (5): 2gamma^2 - gamma_1 - B = gamma^2 - 3gamma_1, so B = gamma^2 + 2gamma_1. Therefore

sum_{n<x} d(n)/n = (gamma + log x)^2 - (1/2) log^2 x + 2gamma_1 + o(1) = (1/2) log^2 x + 2gamma log x + gamma^2 + 2gamma_1 + o(1).

In modern notation the constant is gamma^2 - 2gamma_1(Stieltjes). The next page indicates this belongs with Ramanujan's continuation of 'Highly Composite Numbers'.
errors: No mathematical errors. Every expansion and the final constant gamma^2 + 2gamma_1 (Ramanujan's sign convention) agree with the known result sum_{n<=x} d(n)/n = (1/2)log^2 x + 2gamma log x + gamma^2 - 2gamma_1(Stieltjes) + O(x^{-1/2}).

Unstated step: passing from the convergent series sum a_n/n to the limit of sum a_n/n^s as s->1+ needs Abel's (Dirichlet-series) theorem. It is valid here because (6) and (7) imply convergence. The previous page's analogous step needed a stronger input, the prime number theorem, which Ramanujan does flag there.
Only convergence of sum (2gamma + log n - d(n))/n is needed, so any error term O(x^theta) with theta<1 in the divisor problem would suffice. Dirichlet's O(sqrt x) is more than enough.
Sign convention: Ramanujan's gamma_1 = -gamma_1 of Stieltjes/modern usage. This is consistent throughout the page.

results.modern_name: First Stieltjes constant (Laurent expansion of zeta at s=1)
results.usually_credited_to: Stieltjes (1885), Jensen (1887); numerical value by Gram (1895)

results.what: sum_{n<x} d(n)/n = (1/2)log^2 x + 2gamma log x + gamma^2 + 2gamma_1(Ramanujan's sign) + o(1)
results.modern_name: Asymptotic for the logarithmic mean of the divisor function (constant gamma^2 - 2gamma_1 in Stieltjes normalization)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical, following from Dirichlet's divisor theorem (1849) by partial summation; the explicit constant appears in standard texts (Landau era)

results.what: Method: identify the constant term of a partial sum by matching it with the Laurent constant of the Dirichlet series at s=1 (Abelian argument)
results.modern_name: Abel's theorem for Dirichlet series / comparison of Laurent coefficients

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, neat but routine derivation of a classical constant. Stieltjes constants and divisor-sum asymptotics are known to appear in Ramanujan's notebooks (Berndt, Part I, Ch. 8) and in his highly composite numbers work. The 14-15 digit value of gamma_1 matches Gram's known computation and is not new.
